headline: Medium risk: shared filesystem and overlapping write surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and edit-conflict pathways between ctx and GitHub Copilot.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and touches filesystem/MCP-related context, while GitHub Copilot reads repo context and editor buffers. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if ctx writes or surfaces untrusted text into files Copilot consumes. The pair lacks explicit provenance isolation, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF ctx writes attacker-controlled text into files or logs that Copilot reads as repo context
IF Copilot Workspace or chat consumes those files without provenance filtering
mitigations: Keep ctx outputs in a separate directory not indexed by Copilot
Disable Copilot Workspace on repositories containing ctx-generated artifacts
Add a manual review step before copying ctx output into editor buffers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to ctx-generated files
requires-engineering: enforce file-level isolation between agent outputs and Copilot inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches harness records, graph data, and audit/runtime logs, while Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive ctx-managed data lands in shared files or buffers, Copilot can transmit it to a third party. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, but the filesystem overlap makes leakage plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF ctx stores harness records or audit logs in a repository or editor-visible path
IF Copilot is allowed to read that path as repo context or open buffers
mitigations: Exclude logs and harness records from the repo
Add .gitignore rules for ctx-generated sensitive files
Use a separate workspace for Copilot-assisted editing
Review Copilot context before accepting suggestions
requires-engineering: configure path-based redaction for Copilot inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and use filesystem/MCP-adjacent automation, while Copilot can write filesystem edits and modify git state. Both support multiple instances, but neither profile shows locking or coordination. Concurrent edits to the same repo or files can conflict in default developer workflows, though the blast radius is usually recoverable.
conditions: IF ctx and Copilot operate on the same repository or working tree
IF both are allowed to write overlapping files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or worktree
Pause one agent while the other applies edits
Review git diff before merge
Use file ownership conventions for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management agent that observes tool events, and Copilot Workspace/chat proposes edits for human review. If ctx-produced summaries or facts are fed into Copilot as authoritative repo context, Copilot may propagate errors into code changes. Human review reduces but does not eliminate the cascade, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF ctx-generated summaries are inserted into Copilot-visible context
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits based on those summaries without independent verification
mitigations: Require source links for ctx-generated claims
Cross-check Copilot edits against original files
Limit ctx output to metadata, not assertions
Reject edits that lack traceable provenance
requires-engineering: add verification gates before Copilot applies Workspace edits

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state conflicting residency or certification regimes. The only concrete compliance signal is Copilot's GitHub repo-context/OAuth usage and ctx's audit/runtime logs, which could matter if regulated data is placed there. Because no explicit mismatch is documented, this is a low, conditional compliance concern rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx audit/runtime logs or repo context
IF Copilot is used on that regulated repository without an approved data-processing arrangement
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared repos
Confirm repository data-handling policy before enabling Copilot
Separate audit logs from code workspaces
Restrict Copilot use on regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both tools
